artworks.title: Winter Wren and Rock Wren
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: Four birds perched on branches and greenery. The largest bird is on the left side along a horizontal branch. The color palette includes earthy browns, greens, and hints of pale blue on the branch moss, with the birds displaying a mix of rich brown and buff tones. One bird is on the left cactus-like branch, another in the center on a vertical branch, one bird is on moss-covered ground in the lower right, and another near the lower center pecking at the moss. The background is cream.

artworks.title: Long-tailed or Dusky Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is an image of two Long-tailed or Dusky Grouse set against a mountainous landscape. The birds are depicted with intricate feather detail and red eye combs, standing on grassy and rocky terrain. The background shows mountain formations in soft tones, with a pale blue sky. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for realistic bird portrayals in natural settings.

artworks.title: Yellow-billed Magpie, Stellers Jay, Ultramarine Jay and Clark's Crow
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image depicts several birds in various positions on branches in a natural setting. The color scheme includes blue, black, white, green, yellow, and brown hues. The birds are positioned within a foliage-filled background, with some interacting with seeds.

artworks.title: Bohemian Chatterer
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two birds perched on a branch with clusters of orange berries and green leaves. The scene depicts two Bohemian Waxwings, showcasing the intricate details of their plumage, including patterns of yellow-tipped tails and red markings on their wings. One bird leans towards the other, suggesting interaction. The foliage around them has a few sprigs bearing clusters of orange berries. The composition is vividly colored, capturing the beauty of avian life in their habitat. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: White-winged Crossbill
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows three birds on a branch with green berries and leaves. The birds are red and black with white wing markings. The color palette includes red, green, black, white, and neutrals. The birds are positioned in the center, with two facing each other and one reaching for berries above them.

artworks.title: Lapland Longspur
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of Lapland Longspurs in a natural landscape. The image shows three birds on a rocky terrain by a body of water with foliage and mountains in the distance. The birds have detailed plumage patterns and coloration. The sky above has a gentle gradient. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed bird and nature renderings.

artworks.title: Iceland or Jer Falcon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two white falcons with black markings. The image depicts two falcons, one flying and the other perched on a rocky ledge. The falcons have white plumage with black markings. The flying falcon has its wings spread wide, showcasing the patterns on its feathers, while the perched falcon appears to be vocalizing with its beak open. The ledge is against a gradient sky of deep blue. The painting captures the majesty and elegance of the birds with attention to detail in their feathers and expressions. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Band-tailed Pigeon
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two band-tailed pigeons perched on a flowering branch. The illustration shows two pigeons with banded tails, sitting on a branch with leaves and flowers. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Rock Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds on a rocky landscape with mountains in the background. The artwork features three rock ptarmigans standing on a rocky outcrop. One bird is white with brown feathers and a red circle around its eye. Another bird has a mix of white and brown feathers. The third bird has brown and gold plumage with intricate markings. The backdrop shows mountains under a blue sky. Grass and shrubs are present in the scene. The composition highlights the unique characteristics of each bird, with subtle color tones emphasizing the ambiance of the scene.

artworks.title: Mountain Mocking-bird and Varied Thrush
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of three birds perched on a branch with green leaves and white berries. The composition features three birds, each displaying intricate detail in plumage and posture. One bird displays a light brown coloration with spots on its chest, captured in mid-stride along a leafy branch. Below it, two birds are depicted in vivid detail—one is turned sideways, revealing orange breast and black head markings, while the other lies on its back showing dark grays and oranges. The leafy branch features clusters of small white berries, and the background is left plain, enhancing the focus on the birds. The detailing and style are reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: American Water Ouzel
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds perched on rocks next to a small waterfall. The perspective is eye level with the birds, offering a detailed view of their plumage. The horizon is high, emphasizing distant hills and depth. Brushstrokes outline the birds' plumage with fine detail. The color palette includes earthy browns for the birds and rocks, and cool tones for the waterfall and hills. The background landscape fades to soft blues and grays.

artworks.title: Cock of the Plains
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting features two birds in a natural setting. The birds are elaborately detailed, with one bird displaying intricate patterns and a distinctive throat sac. The other bird appears more subdued, standing slightly behind the first. The background shows a soft, open landscape with distant mountains under a pale sky. The illustration focuses on the detail of the birds' feathers in a realistic style.

artworks.title: Common Buzzard
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows a buzzard flying towards a rabbit on the ground. The buzzard has brown feathers with some lighter underparts, while the rabbit has brown fur with lighter accents. The color palette includes brown, cream, and gray tones, set against a soft blue sky. The rabbit is positioned at the bottom center, while the buzzard dominates the upper portion as it descends. In the background, there is a river, a few trees, and some structures, indicating a rural setting.

artworks.title: Evening Grosbeak and Spotted Grosbeak
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: There are three large birds perched on branches and a butterfly flying nearby. The top bird has a yellow and black plumage with white accents, the middle bird has an orange breast with black and white wings, and the bird on the left is mostly brown with white patterns. The lowest bird has vibrant yellow and reddish-orange feathers with black and white markings on its wings. The butterfly is orange with darker spots. The color palette includes yellow, orange, brown, black, and white. The top bird perches on a branch extending from the upper right, with the middle bird positioned slightly below to the left. The brown bird is further down on the branch, and the colorful bird is on the bottom branch, looking upwards toward the butterfly at the center.

artworks.title: Sharp-shinned Hawk
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two sharp-shinned hawks perched on branches. The top hawk is holding a small rodent in its talons, while the lower hawk is gazing outward. The hawks have dark plumage on their backs and wings, with a brown and white pattern on their underbellies. Their legs and talons are yellow, contrasting with the background. The branches they are on are detailed. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Lesser Red-poll
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The image shows two birds on a branch with white berries. The birds have brown and red plumage with red caps and pinkish chests. The color scheme includes browns, whites, greens, reds, and pinks. The birds are in the center of the image on branches that go from the top right to the lower left, surrounded by foliage and berries.

artworks.title: Trumpeter Swan
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a trumpeter swan resting among tall grasses. The swan is depicted in a graceful posture with its neck elegantly curved. It is surrounded by lush green tall grasses, showcasing the bird's feathers with great attention to detail. The background consists of softly muted earth tones and subtle shading, amplifying the serene and tranquil atmosphere of the scene. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Scolopaceus Courlan
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a long-legged bird standing in a natural landscape. The image features a bird with intricate feather detailing, particularly on its wings and neck, where a pattern of white spots stands out against darker feathers. Its elongated beak and legs are drawn with precise anatomical accuracy. The background reveals a tranquil river or lake, bordered by gentle rolling hills. The coloration is subtle, using muted tones to create a sense of harmony between the bird and its environment. The overall composition is balanced, with the bird positioned diagonally across the canvas.

artworks.title: Hawk Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This painting depicts two hawk owls perched on branches. One owl is vertical on a branch, gazing into the distance with yellow eyes. The other owl is mid-motion, possibly in flight or preparing to dive, displaying spread wings and detailed feather patterns. The owls have brown plumage with black and white markings. They are set against a neutral background with twisted branches. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon's lifelike bird portrayals.

artworks.title: Ruff-necked Humming-bird
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of hummingbirds interacting with a flowering plant. The image shows two colorful hummingbirds hovering around the blooms of the plant, with delicate, elongated stamens extending outward. The hummingbirds are captured in dynamic poses, showcasing their vibrant plumage and the motion of their wings. Another hummingbird is perched on a nest attached to the plant's stem below the flowers. The plant has a cluster of pink and white flowers, with lush green leaves of varying shades. The style of the painting is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Tengmalm's Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two owls perched on branches. The painting features two owls, one in a resting position with its wings partially open, and the other standing upright with alert eyes gazing at its surroundings. Their plumage is detailed, exhibiting a mix of brown, white, and grey with distinct patterns and markings. The owl facing forward has yellow eyes. The realism in the texture of the feathers and the natural posture of the owls give the painting a lifelike quality.

artworks.title: Snow Goose
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of two geese standing by a body of water. The painting features a pair of geese, with one in white plumage and the other in darker plumage. The white goose has a pink bill and long legs standing on brown ground by the water. The darker goose has a dark brown body with a white head and neck. Both birds are depicted with detailed feathers. The background shows a textured sky with clouds and a blue body of water, suggesting an outdoor setting. This is in the style of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Sharp-tailed Grous
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: The painting depicts two sharp-tailed grouses in a natural setting. The birds have brown and white patterns on their feathers, and are standing in a grassy plain with hills in the background under a clear blue sky. Small plant life with colorful berries is visible in the foreground. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon.

artworks.title: Long-eared Owl
artworks.artist: Robert Havell after John James Audubon
artworks.medium: hand-colored engraving and aquatint on Whatman wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Gift of Mrs. Walter B. James
artworks.description: This is a painting of a long-eared owl perched on a branch. The owl is depicted with elongated ear tufts and orange eyes. The plumage is rendered in earthy tones with intricate patterns of browns, tans, and subtle hints of white. The branch is painted in muted grays. The style is reminiscent of John James Audubon, known for detailed ornithological illustrations.
